clarification_questions: What is supposed to be the focal element in this section?

common_mistakes: Adding tracks when the missing issue is role, contrast, or development.
Trying to fix register/rhythm/density conflicts entirely with EQ and compression.
Editing the only project version without a recoverable alternative.
Judging a section alone rather than through the transition and complete song arc.
copyright_handling: Original paraphrased synthesis; no raw forum post body or long quotation included.
do_not_assume: A common setting or arrangement pattern is correct for this source and song.
A meter, spectrum, forum consensus, or model output proves the perceptual complaint or cause.
The first plausible explanation is the true cause.
logic_pro_steps: Create or show markers for the current song sections.
For the relevant section, list each part’s role, register, activity, and focal priority.
Identify one duplicated or missing role related to the question.
Make only the proposed mute, entrance/exit, voicing, or activity change in a recoverable alternative.
Listen through the transition and full section without watching the tracks.
Restore the previous alternative or region state to undo.

rationale: The immediate issue is too many continuously active parts may exhaust attention. The first experiment tests that explanation while protecting against level, source, arrangement, processing, and monitoring confounds.

recommended_first_experiment.action: Label each part as active, sustained, or punctuating and reduce simultaneous active patterns around the focal element.
recommended_first_experiment.summary: Label each part as active, sustained, or punctuating and reduce simultaneous active patterns around the focal element.
recommended_first_experiment.why_this_first: It changes one high-information variable and can strengthen or weaken competing explanations before a permanent treatment.

starting_points: Change one arrangement dimension at a time: role, entrance/exit, density, register, rhythm, note length, or focal hierarchy.
Make structural edits in a Project Alternative or duplicated region so comparison and recovery remain exact.
Judge through the transition and full section; a momentary solo is not enough to evaluate form or focus.
stop_rule: Stop when the focal role, section purpose, and transition are clear and another change no longer adds a distinct musical function.
teaching_principle: Arrangement allocates listener attention across time; remove or redirect competing roles before asking mixing tools to manufacture clarity.
title: How do I balance active and sustained parts in an arrangement
tradeoffs_and_risks: Simplification can improve focus while reducing desired scale, texture, or genre energy.
More contrast can make transitions feel disconnected if no identity cue carries across.
Register or voicing changes can alter harmony, performance, or emotional meaning.
undo_or_reset: Restore the preserved regions, mutes, levels, voicings, automation, or project alternative and replay the same section.
user_language_aliases: too many continuously active parts may exhaust attention
what_to_listen_for: The focal element and section purpose should become easier to understand without losing the song’s identity or intended energy.
The next transition or arrival should gain contrast rather than merely becoming louder or busier.
Removed or changed layers should have a named consequence; keep them out if no meaningful role is lost.
